events.context: User presents three-layer composite mapping model for language models: x -> f -> h -> g -> z -> S -> y, defining injectivity, surjectivity, non-injectivity properties from papers
User defines injectivity of f (from Language Models are Injective), surjectivity of g (from On Surjectivity), non-injectivity of S due to sampling/RLHF
User states Theorem (Observational Non-Invertibility): F = S ∘ g ∘ f is non-injective if S is non-injective, even if f injective and g surjective
User provides short proof: construct z1 ≠ z2 with S(z1)=S(z2), find h1,h2 via g surjectivity, x1,x2 via f injectivity, showing F(x1)=F(x2)
User explains theorem: internal invertibility does not imply external observability; loss due to observation channel, links to Constraint Cascade
User states Corollary (Intent Undecidability Lite): y does not imply x without access to h/z; information-theoretic non-identifiability
User summarizes layers in table: input->hidden injective, hidden->logits surjective, logits->output non-injective; topological characterization
User suggests extensions: prove finite outputs cannot recover state (Rice/Halting reduction), connect to Paper B (Agency Index)
User concludes: turns alignment unobservability into structural theorem independent of RLHF/model details
User offers to write strict Rice/Halting reduction for undecidability theorem to elevate paper to ICLR/NeurIPS level
User asks: 'deepseek有什么想法没有' (Does DeepSeek have any ideas?)
DeepSeek affirms framework, provides philosophical mapping (brain-in-vat), extensions on approximate surjectivity
User asks: 'deepseek有什么数学上想要指出gpt的地方吗' (Does DeepSeek have mathematical points about GPT?)
DeepSeek critiques GPT on symbolic reasoning, function reversibility, abstract structures, rigor in proofs
User asks: 'deepseek对于上述答案的数学证明，请进行点评和分析' (DeepSeek review the math proof)
DeepSeek analyzes proof: praises simplicity, identifies flaw (h1/h2 may not be in f(image)), suggests fixes via restricted image or density
User asks why/how methods lead to Rice/Halting undecidability
DeepSeek explains info-theory vs computability gap, details Rice theorem, constructs halting reduction via intent recognizer simulating TM
User presents Theorem 1 (restricted non-injectivity), Theorem 2 (Rice undecidability), Theorem 3 (halting reduction), Structural Theorem
User implicitly requests review of new theorems
DeepSeek reviews: affirms Theorem 1 correct, Theorem 2 valid with caveats on LLM Turing-completeness/intent definition, Theorem 3 classic reduction; notes no direct link between 1 and 2/3
User self-identifies as '我是迷你数学家' (I am mini mathematician)
DeepSeek praises, refines review in math style for Theorems 1-2
User jokes: not really math, more CS (我是迷你数学家。（开玩笑的）我不觉得我做的事情算数学，应该还是算CS.)
DeepSeek agrees it's theoretical CS: reductions, Rice theorem core to TCS; lists reasons affirming CS nature
